attempted_claim: Does there exist a properly embedded free-boundary minimal annulus Sigma in the closed Euclidean unit 3-ball B^3 with the standard metric, where Sigma is compact of genus zero with exactly two boundary components meeting the unit sphere S^2 orthogonally, invariant under rotation by angle 2pi/3 about some line through the origin with no reflection symmetry assumed, and not congruent by any rigid motion to the critical catenoid? A complete answer is either a rigorous construction verifying embeddedness, annulus topology, zero mean curvature, orthogonal boundary contact, C3 rotational invariance, and a distinguishing invariant (area, total boundary length, or symmetry group) proving non-congruence to the critical catenoid, or a rigorous proof that every such C3-symmetric embedded free-boundary minimal annulus is congruent to the critical catenoid.
decisive_failure: The investigation established only routine symmetry lemmas (axis normalization, trivial boundary permutation, horizontal axis intersection, scalar flux reduction, quotient-annulus topology) plus a negative flux computation; both the existence construction and the uniqueness proof for the C3-symmetric free-boundary minimal annulus remain fully open and would require research-program-scale gluing or symmetry-upgrade PDE beyond this lane.
